segments.text: 37% of new hires joined their savings plan. Then 86% did.
Same company. Same plan. Only the default changed.
Before, you had to sign up. After, you were signed up unless you opted out.
That was one company, in a 2001 study. And the catch: most of them never raised the low default.
If you save what's left, what's left is often nothing. So make saving your default: schedule a small transfer for payday, then raise it later.
Try it today: schedule one tiny transfer for your next payday.
